Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
651 PM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes to the current forecast package. Latest model 
runs continue to trend drier in regards to precipitation chances 
Thursday through Saturday AM. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) First accumulating snow for parts of the Alleghenies with
  rain showers and brisk conditions elsewhere, Thursday through
  Saturday.

- 2) Cooler temperatures & dry condtions expected for much of
  next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...First accumulating snow for parts of the Alleghenies with rain 
showers and brisk conditions elsewhere, Thursday through Saturday.

No significant changes are expected to the current forecast package 
outside timing of precipitation chances Thursday into Friday. Still 
monitoring an area of low pressure ejecting out of the southern 
Great Lakes/Ohio River Valley and it's associated cold frontal 
boundary that is set to cross late Thursday morning into Thursday 
afternoon. The low will shift off the Delmarva coast Thursday 
evening into Thursday night before pulling away Friday into the 
weekend. A secondary front and piece of shortwave energy will pivot 
through the area Friday into Saturday morning reinforcing the colder 
air along with upslope precipitation over the mountains. 

After a prolonged stretch of dry weather the chance for widespread 
precipitation returns. Unfortunately, this will not be a drought 
buster by any means with QPF values trending downward, especially 
east of the Blue Ridge per the latest model guidance. Most locations 
will see a tenth of an inch or less in the precipitation department 
Thursday through Saturday. Higher amounts of precipitation will be 
noted over northeast MD and the Catoctins where a tenth to a quarter 
of an inch of precipitation are expected. The highest precipitation 
totals will be in the upslope areas of the Alleghenies with 
widespread amounts of a quarter to a half an inch expected. Most of 
this will come in the form of snow late Thursday night into Friday 
as colder air wraps in. 

Speaking of snow, this will be the first flakes and accumulation of 
the season for portions of the Allegheny Mountains. Accumulations 
will likely remain just shy of advisory criteria due largely in part 
to marginal temperatures at the onset and during the during the 
duration of the event. Most locations will see a coating-2" above 
2000 feet with 2-3" at elevations above 3500 feet. Locally higher 
totals are possible along Backbone Mountain at Hoyes Crest and down 
toward Spruce Knob pending the orientation of any streamer activity 
off of Lake Erie/Lake Michigan Friday night into Saturday morning. 
This will be the time window of greatest impact on high elevation 
roadways given temperatures below freezing. Roadways impacted 
included US-219 from Keysers Ridge south into WV, US-48 west of 
Bismarck/Mt. Storm, WV, US-33 west of Franklin, WV, and US-250 west 
of Monterey, VA. Expect temperatures in the 20s leading to fluffier 
snow characters with ratios of 13:1 or better. 

High temperatures Thursday will range from the upper 40s over the 
mountains to low 60s near the bay. Temperatures tumble Thursday 
evening with lows Thursday night in the 30s and 40s. Winds crank up 
out of the west and northwest Thursday afternoon and evening 
continuing through Friday with gusts between 20-30 mph. Locally 
higher gusts are possible along the ridges. These winds will yield 
wind chills in the 30s and 40s for both Friday and Saturday with air 
temperatures outside the mountains struggling to get out of the 
upper 40s and low 50s in most locations. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler temperatures & dry condtions expected 
for much of next week. 

As the weekend's longwave trough slowly pushes offshore early next 
week, winds could remain elevated through Sunday before diminishing 
between Monday & Tuesday in the wake of the cold front. Temperatures 
are likely to remain much cooler areawide throughout the week, with 
many areas seeing near or below freezing temperatures overnight 
beginning this weekend through the remainder of the forecast period.

Overall, generally calm, clear conditions persist throughout the 
week as a upper-level ridging transitions overhead. Daytime 
temperatures moderate a bit later in the week with continued high 
pressure, with afternoon highs in the mid-to-upper 50s on
Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
VFR conditions will continue this evening with light winds out of 
the south and southwest at less than 10 kts. Mid and high level 
cloud cover will continue to increase as a wave of low pressure and 
cold front eject east from the southern Great Lakes/Ohio River 
Valley. This system will bring pockets of light rain to the 
terminals on and off throughout Thursday. Shower activity should 
push into terminals west of MRB prior 13z/8am before advancing east 
toward the corridor late Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon. 
Activity will be scattered and light in nature leading to more in 
the way of cig reductions compared to vsbys. 

Wind will become the bigger issue for aviation Thursday afternoon 
and continuing through Saturday. Expect gusts on the order of 20-30 
kts out of the northwest with locally higher gusts over the ridges 
and waters. Winds will be reinforced out of the northwest Friday 
into Saturday as another ripple of energy pulses through. A spotty 
sprinkle is possible east of the mountains Friday although most 
terminals outside of those west of KCBE will be dry. VFR conditions 
are expected Friday into the weekend outside of the mountains where 
upslope snow showers will persists. 

VFR conditions are expected to continue into early next week. Winds 
diminish Sunday into Monday while shifting northerly Tuesday into 
midweek as high pressure settles over the region. 

&&

.MARINE...
Sub-SCA level winds are expected to continue overnight ahead of an 
approaching cold frontal boundary. SCA conditions are likely 
Thursday afternoon through Saturday as a wave of low pressure and 
series of fronts cross the waters. Expect north to northwesterly 
winds to gusts 20-30 kts at times Thursday evening and throughout 
Friday into Saturday.  Winds likely start to diminish back below SCA 
levels Sunday and Monday, shifting more northerly by Tuesday. Sub-
SCA level conditions are expected with high pressure for the middle 
of the next week. 


&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Action Stages are likely Thursday night before winds shift to 
northwest behind a cold front. A strong frontal passage will 
bring a prolonged period of blowout tides Friday and through 
early next week.
